definition: Finding items whose vector embeddings are closest to a query, rather than matching exact keywords.
details: Text, images and other data are embedded into high-dimensional vectors, and approximate nearest-neighbor indexes retrieve the most similar ones at scale. It powers semantic search, recommendation and retrieval-augmented generation.

explainer.lead: Vector search retrieves items whose embeddings are closest to a query rather than matching exact keywords. It matters because it enables semantic retrieval at scale.

tiers.eli5: Instead of looking for the exact word, you look for things that mean the same thing and sit nearby on a giant map of meanings.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers embed text and images into high-dimensional vectors and query approximate nearest-neighbor indexes. A pitfall is that approximate indexes trade recall for speed, so results can miss the true nearest items.
tiers.paperLevel: Data is embedded into high-dimensional vectors and an approximate nearest-neighbor index returns the closest ones. Approximation means exact nearest neighbors are not guaranteed.

explainer.example: A query about 'cheap flights to Rome' returns documents about budget airfare even though they never use the word 'cheap'.
